description: Golden set for the bundled corpus. Ground truth is a source file plus a substring the correct passage must contain, so cases survive re-chunking and re-indexing. Every 'contains' value is verified against the corpus by `ragkit eval --verify`, which runs in CI.

kinds.exact-id: Opaque identifiers, codes, and header names. Embeddings have no meaning to encode for these, so this is where the lexical arm should carry the query.
kinds.paraphrase: Natural questions sharing few or no words with the passage that answers them. The dense arm's home ground; lexical should miss most of these outright.
kinds.table: The answer lives inside a markdown table. Fails outright if chunking splits tables, which is what makes these worth separating out.
kinds.discriminate: Terms that appear in more than one document. Tests whether retrieval picks the right context rather than merely the right keyword.

cases.why: A bare document identifier with no semantic content whatsoever.

cases.query: which policy does POL-3980 replace
cases.why: Identifier embedded in a natural question — needs both arms to cooperate.

cases.query: SPRING24
cases.why: Promo code appearing exactly once, in an exceptions section.

cases.query: EXP-2DA cutoff time
cases.why: The one query dense retrieval demoted to rank 2 before the lexical arm existed.

cases.query: X-Signature header
cases.why: An HTTP header name: hyphenated, capitalised, and meaningless to an embedding.

cases.query: idempotency_key
cases.why: Snake_case field name. Tokenisation splits it, which is worth exercising.

cases.query: how long do I have to return an international order?
cases.why: The answer is one row of a table. If chunking split it, the row arrives without its header and this fails.

cases.query: what is the restocking fee for clearance items
cases.why: Requires reading across columns of the same row.

cases.query: latest I can order for next business day delivery
cases.why: Paraphrase whose answer is a table cell — needs dense retrieval to reach a table.

cases.query: error code 1005

relevant.contains: Idempotency key reused with different body

cases.why: Numeric code in a table. The number alone is a weak embedding signal.

cases.query: what happens if my package shows up broken
cases.why: 'broken' never appears in the passage; 'damaged' does.

cases.query: do you train models on my support conversations

relevant.contains: not used to train any model

cases.why: Close paraphrase of the heading, which the heading-path fold should help with.

cases.query: when does the refund clock start counting

relevant.contains: delivery date recorded by the carrier

cases.why: 'clock' appears nowhere in the corpus. Purely semantic.

cases.query: can I send it back if I opened the box
cases.why: Colloquial phrasing against formal policy language.

cases.query: how fast until money is back on my card
cases.why: The passage says 'card refunds typically appear'; the query says 'money is back'.

cases.query: which staff can look at my card number
cases.why: The answer uses 'payment instrument', a phrase no user would type.

cases.query: what if nobody is home when the freight arrives
cases.why: Situational question against a policy statement.

cases.query: how quickly would you tell me if you got hacked
cases.why: 'hacked' is colloquial; the passage says 'breach'.

cases.query: which country are my records kept in
cases.why: Answer is a city name; question asks about a country.

cases.query: how long before a parcel counts as lost

relevant.contains: fifteen business days with no tracking movement

cases.why: Day-count windows appear in both refunds and shipping. Keyword matching alone lands in the wrong document.

cases.query: how long do you keep my data after I close my account
cases.why: 'how long' plus a duration also matches refund windows and shipping transit times.

cases.query: what limit applies per minute
cases.why: 'limit' and time units appear in shipping cutoffs and refund windows too.
